chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who dies an apostate from Islam, and he has children, so he said: His wealth is for his Muslim children.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits the estate of an apostate in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that apostasy does not sever the blood ties (qaraba) for inheritance purposes, a key distinction in Shia fiqh where the apostate's estate passes to his Muslim offspring. This ruling contrasts with some Sunni schools that may withhold inheritance from apostates, emphasizing the Shia view that the father-child relationship remains intact despite the change in the father's religious status.
